approach.summary: Add a `json` bool flag to cmdStats. Keep the existing loop that accumulates the totals, but skip the tabwriter writes when --json is set and collect one row struct per run instead. After the loop, in JSON mode, build a totals struct from the values already computed (tot, byStatus, damaged, partial, and the two 'at least' conditions). Marshal {runs, totals} with json.MarshalIndent(…, "", " "), print it with Fprintln and return. The text path stays byte-for-byte the same. Update the usage line and the README row. Test the JSON output in three places: exact values and zero-valued keys on the existing fixture, which has a damaged run (both lower bounds true); a complete-usage fixture (both lower bounds false); and incomplete-only and unknown-only fixtures without a damaged run (spend false, usage true).

steps.title: Add --json output to cmdStats
steps.objective: `shogun stats --json` prints the runs and totals as one JSON document, and the text output stays the same.
actions: In stats.go, import "encoding/json". After the --dir flag, add `asJSON := fs.Bool("json", false, "print runs and totals as JSON on stdout")`.

Define the JSON types next to runStats. statsRow has json tags id, status and damaged (omitempty string) and embeds a *statsCounts pointer. statsCounts holds mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd and usage. None of these tags use omitempty, so zero values stay visible. The pointer is nil for a damaged run, which leaves those fields out. statsTotals holds runs, by_status (map[string]int), damaged, attempts, active_seconds, the five token sums, cost_usd, usage_incomplete_runs, usage_unknown_runs, spend_lower_bound and usage_lower_bound, all without omitempty.

In the existing loop, guard each fmt.Fprintf/Fprintln(tw, …), header line included, with `if !*asJSON`. Append one statsRow per run. For a damaged run: {id, "damaged", r.damaged, nil}. For a readable run: {id, string(r.st.Status), "", &statsCounts{mode, r.planner, r.reviewer, the counters…, u}}. Leave the accumulation of tot, byStatus, damaged and partial unchanged.

After the loop, if *asJSON: build statsTotals from len(runs), byStatus, damaged, tot, partial["incomplete"] and partial["unknown"]. Set spend_lower_bound = damaged > 0 and usage_lower_bound = len(partial) > 0 || damaged > 0. Marshal struct{Runs []statsRow `json:"runs"`; Totals statsTotals `json:"totals"`} with json.MarshalIndent(v, "", " "), Fprintln it to a.stdout and return ExitOK. Otherwise, continue into the unchanged tw.Flush() and totals text. Keep the empty-runs early return (stderr message) as it is (Q-001).
Update the stats usage line in main.go:87 to `shogun stats [--dir d] [--json]` and keep the column alignment. In the stats row at README.md:237, add `, `--json`` after `--dir`.

verification.expected: `go build ./... && go vet ./cmd/shogun` succeed, and `gofmt -l cmd/shogun` prints nothing.

The git diff of stats.go leaves the header string, the row format strings and the totals Fprintf lines unchanged. They are only wrapped in `if !*asJSON` or come after the JSON early return (R-002.C1).

steps.title: Test the JSON output: exact values, zero keys and both lower-bound flags
steps.objective: Show that the JSON document holds every field of the table and totals with exact values, that the two lower-bound flags follow their separate rules, that the text output still passes, and that nothing is written.
actions: Add "encoding/json" to the imports. At the end of TestStatsCountsEveryRunAndFlagsMissingUsage, after the existing assertions (which stay unchanged), call runCLI(t, ws, "stats", "--json") and require ExitOK.

Assert that out contains neither "STATUS" nor "total:". Then json.Unmarshal the whole of out into map[string]any. Unmarshal rejects trailing data, so success means exactly one document. Numbers compare as float64.

Run 20260927-000001-a must contain all 14 keys (id, status, mode, planner, reviewer, attempts, active_seconds, input_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_usd, usage), with these exact values: approved, fast, claude/opus:high, codex/gpt-6-astra:high, 2, 150, 100, 1000, 0 (the key must be present), 50, 20, 0.5, ok. Run 20260927-000002-b: usage unknown and cost_usd key present with 0. Run 20260927-000003-c: status damaged, a non-empty damaged field and no attempts key.

Totals must equal exactly: runs 5; by_status {approved:1, failed:1, needs_input:1, paused:1}; damaged 1; attempts 6; active_seconds 750; input_tokens 100; cache_read_tokens 1000; cache_write_tokens 0 (key present); output_tokens 50; reasoning_tokens 20; cost_usd 0.5; usage_incomplete_runs 0 (key present); usage_unknown_runs 1; spend_lower_bound true; usage_lower_bound true.
Re-read 20260927-000001-a/state.json after the --json call and compare it with `before`.

Add a table-driven TestStatsJSONLowerBounds. Each case gets a fresh HOME and ws (t.TempDir) and creates runs with run.Create, run.NewState and SaveState under run.RunsRoot(ws), with no damaged run, then parses `stats --json`. Case 'complete': two approved runs with distinct non-zero counters, {Attempts 1, ActiveSeconds 60, Input 10, CacheRead 20, CacheWrite 30, Output 40, Reasoning 5, Cost 0.25} and {Attempts 3, ActiveSeconds 30, Input 1, CacheRead 2, CacheWrite 3, Output 4, Reasoning 1, Cost 0.125}. Expect totals attempts 4, active_seconds 90, input 11, cache_read 22, cache_write 33, output 44, reasoning 6, cost_usd 0.375, damaged 0, usage_incomplete_runs 0, usage_unknown_runs 0, spend_lower_bound false, usage_lower_bound false. Case 'incomplete': one run {Attempts 2, Input 5, Output 5, UsageIncomplete true}. Expect usage_incomplete_runs 1, usage_unknown_runs 0, spend_lower_bound false, usage_lower_bound true. Case 'unknown': one run {Attempts 1}. Expect usage_incomplete_runs 0, usage_unknown_runs 1, spend_lower_bound false, usage_lower_bound true.

verification.expected: `go test ./cmd/shogun -run TestStatsCountsEveryRunAndFlagsMissingUsage` passes. This covers the unchanged table assertions (R-002.C1); single-document parsing without table text (R-001.C1); all run keys, including zero-valued ones, with exact values (R-001.C2); the damaged run object (R-001.C3); exact totals with both flags true (R-001.C4); and an unchanged state.json after --json (R-003.C1).

`go test ./cmd/shogun -run TestStatsJSONLowerBounds` passes all three cases. The complete case has exact token and cost sums with both flags false. The incomplete and unknown cases without a damaged run have spend_lower_bound false and usage_lower_bound true (R-001.C4).

responses_to_findings.note: S-002 now asserts all 14 keys of a readable run with exact values, including the zero-valued cache_write_tokens and cost_usd keys. It also asserts every totals field exactly (all five token sums, cost_usd 0.5, usage_incomplete_runs 0 as a present key). A new table-driven TestStatsJSONLowerBounds covers three cases without a damaged run: complete usage, with distinct non-zero counters so a mis-mapped field fails, exact sums and both flags false; incomplete-only; and unknown-only, each with spend_lower_bound false and usage_lower_bound true. The mechanical problem is also fixed: R-003 is removed from S-001's requirement_ids, since R-003.C1 is checked only in S-002.
